title: Molecular Genetic Analysis of the Rabies Virus in Wild and Domestic Animals of Kazakhstan and the Development of a Diagnostic System
abstract: Rabies remains one of the most significant zoonotic infections, characterized by high mortality. In Kazakhstan, the virus circulates among both domestic and wild animals, necessitating ongoing molecular genetic monitoring and improved laboratory diagnostic methods. The aim of this study was to investigate the genetic characteristics of the rabies virus circulating among animals in Kazakhstan using nucleoprotein (N) gene analysis and to develop a regionally adapted real-time RT-PCR method for its detection. Kazakhstani rabies virus isolates deposited in GenBank revealed that all belong to a cosmopolitan lineage and form a single phylogenetic cluster, regardless of host species. Isolates from neighboring countries, including China and Russia, were also included in this cluster, demonstrating the regional relationship of circulating virus variants. The obtained data were used to develop a real-time PCR method based on the genetic characteristics of the rabies virus circulating in Kazakhstan. The diagnostic performance of the method was evaluated using 144 samples of various origins obtained from domestic and wild animals, including bats. The developed assay demonstrated a sensitivity of 86.4%, a specificity of 98.4%, and a diagnostic efficiency of 96.5%. The proposed method ensures reliable detection of rabies virus variants circulating in Kazakhstan and can be used for laboratory diagnostics and epidemiological monitoring.

title: Psychological effects of rabies on the relatives of people who died from human rabies in Côte d'Ivoire between 2023 and 2025: Qualitative Observational Study
abstract: Abstract Background : the psychological impact of rabies on the relatives of people who died from the disease remains largely unexplored. The aim of this study was to analyse the psychological effects of rabies on the relatives of people who died from human rabies in Côte d’Ivoire. Patients and methods : A single-center descriptive study was conducted from January to June 2026 using a qualitative approach, enabled an in-depth exploration of the experiences of these relatives. The participants, aged at least 18 years, were relatives of people who died from confirmed or suspected human rabies between 2023 and 2025, identified from the death notification register of the Anti-Rabies Center of the National Institute of Public Hygiene. The data were collected by individual semi-structured interviews conducted until data saturation was achieved, then subjected to a thematic analysis. Faced with the announcement of the diagnosis and its fatal prognosis, sadness (18/37), helplessness (15/37), anger (8/37) and shock (9/37), feelings of abandonment (1/37) and guilt (7/37) were the predominant emotional responses. After death, relatives reported almost universal intrusive memories, sleep disturbances (24/37), nightmares (15/37) and avoidance of animals (11/37), suggestive of post-traumatic psychological distress and prolonged grief, aggravated by the disruption of traditional funeral practices. Coping relied almost exclusively on prayer (28/37), and family and community support (18/37), with no participant reporting receipt of any formal psychological support. Conclusion : The burden of rabies extends beyond mortality and includes profound and lasting psychological suffering among the relatives of people who die from human rabies. The integration of a culturally appropriate psychosocial component into rabies management would help relieve families and strengthen awareness towards achieving the goal of eliminating rabies by 2030.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The psychological impact of rabies on relatives of deceased patients remains largely unexplored, creating a knowledge gap in understanding the broader burden of human rabies beyond mortality. The study aimed to analyse the psychological effects experienced by relatives of people who died from human rabies in Côte d'Ivoire.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A single-center descriptive qualitative study was conducted from January to June 2026 among relatives of individuals who died from confirmed or suspected human rabies between 2023 and 2025, identified through the death notification register of the Anti-Rabies Center of the National Institute of Public Hygiene.
analysis.methods: Individual semi-structured interviews were conducted until data saturation was achieved, and the data were subjected to thematic analysis to explore the psychological experiences of the relatives.
analysis.main_results: Relatives reported predominant emotional responses including sadness (18/37), helplessness (15/37), anger (8/37), shock (9/37), feelings of abandonment (1/37), and guilt (7/37). After death, intrusive memories, sleep disturbances (24/37), nightmares (15/37), and avoidance of animals (11/37) were almost universally reported, suggestive of post-traumatic psychological distress and prolonged grief.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that the burden of rabies extends beyond mortality to include profound and lasting psychological suffering among relatives, with coping relying almost exclusively on prayer (28/37) and family/community support (18/37) rather than formal psychological assistance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the need to integrate culturally appropriate psychosocial support into rabies management to address the psychological suffering of affected families and strengthen awareness toward the 2030 rabies elimination goal.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-center, qualitative design limits generalisability, and the absence of formal psychological support reporting may reflect local service gaps rather than universal lack of access, warranting cautious interpretation of the evidence strength as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative observational study in Côte d'Ivoire examined the psychological effects on relatives of people who died from human rabies between 2023 and 2025. Using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis, the research identified predominant emotional responses such as sadness, helplessness, anger, and shock, alongside post-traumatic symptoms including intrusive memories, sleep disturbances, nightmares, and avoidance behaviors. Coping mechanisms were almost exclusively informal, relying on prayer and family/community support, with no reported formal psychological assistance. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that rabies imposes a profound and lasting psychological burden beyond mortality. They recommend integrating culturally appropriate psychosocial components into rabies management to support affected families and advance rabies elimination goals by 2030. The single-center design and qualitative approach limit generalisability, and the lack of formal support reporting may reflect local service gaps rather than universal absence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 狂犬病 对已故患者亲属的心理影响在很大程度上仍未被探索,这在理解 狂犬病 除 死亡率 之外的人类 狂犬病 更广泛的负担方面造成了知识差距。该研究旨在分析科特迪瓦死于人类 狂犬病 的人的亲属所经历的心理影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项单中心描述性定性研究于2026年1月至6月在人狂犬病(2023年至2025年确诊或疑似病例的亲属)中开展,研究对象通过国家公共卫生研究院抗狂犬病中心的死亡通知登记系统识别。
elements_zh.methods: 进行个体半结构化访谈直至数据饱和,并对数据进行主题分析,探讨亲属的心理经历。
elements_zh.main_results: 亲属报告的主要情绪反应包括悲伤(18/37)、无助(15/37)、愤怒(8/37)、震惊(9/37)、被遗弃感(1/37)和内疚(7/37)。死亡后,侵入性记忆、睡眠障碍(24/37)、噩梦(15/37)和回避动物(11/37)几乎普遍报道,表明创伤后心理困扰和长期悲伤。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究强调,狂犬病的负担不仅限于死亡率,还包括家属长期且深重的心理痛苦。应对方式几乎完全依赖祈祷(28/37)和家庭/社区支持(18/37),而非正式的心理援助。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果凸显需将文化适宜的心理社会支持纳入狂犬病管理,以应对受影响家庭的心理痛苦,并加强对2030年消除狂犬病目标的认知。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 单中心、定性设计限制了研究结果的普遍性;正式心理支持报告的缺失可能反映当地服务缺口而非普遍缺乏获取途径,因此证据强度应谨慎解读为中等。

title: Atypical neuroimaging in rabies encephalitis: A case report of concurrent cerebral venous sinus thrombosis in a nine-year-old patient
abstract: Human rabies is a fatal viral encephalitis that presents a profound diagnostic challenge in the absence of a known history of animal exposure. We report the case of a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with fever, seizures, psychomotor agitation, hypersalivation and hydrophobia, despite no reported history of an animal bite or scratch. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) served as a critical diagnostic tool, strongly suggesting rabies encephalitis by revealing classic bilateral symmetric grey matter hyperintensities in the thalami and temporal lobes. Concurrently, MRI revealed an atypical and rare macrovascular finding: extensive cerebral venous sinus thrombosis of the right transverse and sigmoid sinuses, which likely accounted for additional asymmetric white matter changes. A nuchal skin biopsy analyzed via reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction confirmed the presence of rabies virus RNA. Despite aggressive neurocritical care and therapeutic anticoagulation, the patient's condition deteriorated, and he passed away on day 9 of admission. This case underscores the dual role of MRI in acute encephalitis: guiding early etiological diagnosis of rabies and identifying concurrent, clinically significant macrovascular complications like cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human rabies is a uniformly fatal encephalitis that poses diagnostic challenges when exposure history is absent, creating uncertainty in early clinical recognition and management.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This single-patient case report describes a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with fever, seizures, psychomotor agitation, hypersalivation, and hydrophobia without a reported animal exposure history.
analysis.methods: Diagnostic evaluation included brain MRI to identify encephalitic changes and a nuchal skin biopsy analyzed by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction for rabies virus RNA confirmation.
analysis.main_results: MRI revealed bilateral symmetric grey matter hyperintensities in the thalami and temporal lobes consistent with rabies encephalitis and an atypical finding of extensive cerebral venous sinus thrombosis involving the right transverse and sigmoid sinuses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the MRI as demonstrating the dual diagnostic role of imaging in rabies—supporting early etiological diagnosis while simultaneously identifying a rare macrovascular complication, cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This case highlights the importance of MRI in acute encephalitis for both etiological diagnosis of rabies and detection of concurrent macrovascular complications that may influence management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a single case report with no control group, restricting generalizability and precluding causal inference; the strength of evidence is low.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with clinical features of rabies encephalitis despite no reported animal exposure. Brain MRI showed classic bilateral thalamic and temporal lobe hyperintensities suggestive of rabies and an atypical finding of right transverse and sigmoid sinus thrombosis. Rabies virus RNA was confirmed by RT-PCR from a nuchal skin biopsy. Despite intensive care and anticoagulation, the patient died on day 9. The authors emphasize MRI’s dual diagnostic utility in rabies—identifying encephalitic changes and concurrent macrovascular complications—but the single-case design limits broader conclusions.

elements_zh.methods: 诊断评估包括用于识别脑炎变化的脑部 MRI 以及通过逆转录聚合酶链反应进行颈项皮肤活检分析以确认 狂犬病病毒 RNA。
elements_zh.main_results: MRI 显示丘脑和颞叶双侧对称灰质高信号,与 狂犬病 脑炎一致,并且非典型发现广泛的脑静脉窦血栓形成累及右侧横窦和乙状窦。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将MRI解释为展示了狂犬病影像学的双重诊断作用——支持早期病因学诊断的同时,还识别出一种罕见的大血管并发症(脑静脉窦血栓形成)。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本病例强调了MRI在急性脑炎中的重要性,既可用于狂犬病的病因学诊断,又能检测可能影响治疗的并发性大血管并发症。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本证据仅限于单例病例报告且无对照组,限制了结果的普遍性并无法推断因果关系;证据强度较低。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Human rabies is a uniformly fatal encephalitis that poses diagnostic challenges when exposure history is absent, creating uncertainty in early clinical recognition and management.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This single-patient case report describes a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with fever, seizures, psychomotor agitation, hypersalivation, and hydrophobia without a reported animal exposure history.
analysis_en.methods: Diagnostic evaluation included brain MRI to identify encephalitic changes and a nuchal skin biopsy analyzed by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction for rabies virus RNA confirmation.
analysis_en.main_results: MRI revealed bilateral symmetric grey matter hyperintensities in the thalami and temporal lobes consistent with rabies encephalitis and an atypical finding of extensive cerebral venous sinus thrombosis involving the right transverse and sigmoid sinuses.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the MRI as demonstrating the dual diagnostic role of imaging in rabies—supporting early etiological diagnosis while simultaneously identifying a rare macrovascular complication, cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This case highlights the importance of MRI in acute encephalitis for both etiological diagnosis of rabies and detection of concurrent macrovascular complications that may influence management.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a single case report with no control group, restricting generalizability and precluding causal inference; the strength of evidence is low.

title_zh: 狂犬病 脑炎的非典型神经影像:一名 9 岁患者并发脑静脉窦血栓形成的 病例报告
source_body_en: Human rabies is a fatal viral encephalitis that presents a profound diagnostic challenge in the absence of a known history of animal exposure. We report the case of a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with fever, seizures, psychomotor agitation, hypersalivation and hydrophobia, despite no reported history of an animal bite or scratch. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) served as a critical diagnostic tool, strongly suggesting rabies encephalitis by revealing classic bilateral symmetric grey matter hyperintensities in the thalami and temporal lobes. Concurrently, MRI revealed an atypical and rare macrovascular finding: extensive cerebral venous sinus thrombosis of the right transverse and sigmoid sinuses, which likely accounted for additional asymmetric white matter changes. A nuchal skin biopsy analyzed via reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction confirmed the presence of rabies virus RNA. Despite aggressive neurocritical care and therapeutic anticoagulation, the patient's condition deteriorated, and he passed away on day 9 of admission. This case underscores the dual role of MRI in acute encephalitis: guiding early etiological diagnosis of rabies and identifying concurrent, clinically significant macrovascular complications like cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.
abstract_zh: 人类狂犬病是一种致命的病毒性脑炎,在缺乏已知动物接触史的情况下,其诊断极具挑战性。我们报告了一例来自摩洛哥的9岁男童病例,该患者出现发热、癫痫发作、精神运动性激越、流涎及恐水症,但未报告有动物咬伤或抓伤史。脑磁共振成像(MRI)作为关键诊断工具,通过显示典型的双侧对称性丘脑和颞叶灰质高信号,强烈提示狂犬病脑炎。同时,MRI还显示了一种罕见的大血管异常发现:右侧横窦和乙状窦广泛性脑静脉窦血栓形成,这可能解释了额外的不对称性白质改变。枕部皮肤活检通过逆转录聚合酶链反应确认了狂犬病病毒 RNA的存在。尽管采取了积极的神经重症监护和治疗性抗凝,患者病情仍恶化,并于入院第9天死亡。本病例强调了MRI在急性脑炎中的双重作用:指导早期病因学诊断狂犬病,并识别并发的、具有临床意义的大血管并发症(如脑静脉窦血栓形成)。

title: 5' untranslated region (5' UTR) of bovine β-globin in the mRNA constructs translates different types of antigenic proteins.
abstract: Synthetic messenger RNA (mRNA) is emerging as next generation vaccine platform. As natural 5'UTRs of particular genes do not work for other than its own mRNA, it is essential to identify an ideal 5'UTR supporting higher translation efficiency for different antigens. Six natural 5'UTRs derived from α, β-globin genes of host animals and other viral genes were cloned upstream to the coding sequences of reporter proteins. The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription and the translation efficiency was assessed using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments. The results revealed higher translation of reporter proteins by bovine β-globin 5'UTR in different cell lines. Further, the chosen 5'UTR supported mRNA translation to produce different antigenic proteins such as rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), major structural protein of foot and mouth disease virus (VP1) and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx). Bovine -globin 5'UTR not only increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins but also supported the expression of different antigenic proteins. Hence, bovine -globin 5'UTR can be used in the mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases.

analysis.methods: The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription and the translation efficiency was assessed using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective mRNA vaccines against rabies virus and rabies infection. The study provides a potential tool for enhancing translation efficiency in mRNA constructs for various antigenic proteins.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its use of different cell lines and the absence of in vivo testing. The evidence is moderate as it is based on in vitro experiments and does not include clinical or epidemiological data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential of the bovine β-globin 5'UTR as a universal enhancer for mRNA translation efficiency in vaccine development. The research aimed to address the challenge of using natural 5'UTRs, which are gene-specific, by evaluating synthetic mRNA constructs with different 5'UTRs. The authors cloned six natural 5'UTRs from various sources and assessed their impact on translation efficiency using in vitro methods. The results showed that the bovine β-globin 5'UTR significantly enhanced the translation of reporter proteins and supported the expression of different antigenic proteins, including rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG). The study suggests that this 5'UTR could be a valuable component in mRNA vaccine designs targeting rabies virus and related diseases. However, the findings are based on in vitro experiments and lack in vivo validation, which limits their applicability to real-world scenarios. The evidence is moderate, as it does not include clinical or epidemiological data.

title_zh: mRNA 构建体中牛 β-珠蛋白的 5' 非翻译区 (5' UTR) 可翻译不同类型的抗原蛋白。
source_body_en: Synthetic messenger RNA (mRNA) is emerging as next generation vaccine platform. As natural 5'UTRs of particular genes do not work for other than its own mRNA, it is essential to identify an ideal 5'UTR supporting higher translation efficiency for different antigens. Six natural 5'UTRs derived from α, β-globin genes of host animals and other viral genes were cloned upstream to the coding sequences of reporter proteins. The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription and the translation efficiency was assessed using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments. The results revealed higher translation of reporter proteins by bovine β-globin 5'UTR in different cell lines. Further, the chosen 5'UTR supported mRNA translation to produce different antigenic proteins such as rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), major structural protein of foot and mouth disease virus (VP1) and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx). Bovine -globin 5'UTR not only increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins but also supported the expression of different antigenic proteins. Hence, bovine -globin 5'UTR can be used in the mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases.

title: Temporal trends and determinants of delayed care-seeking after rabies exposure: a 27,930-patient analysis in Tianjin
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Prompt care-seeking after rabies exposure is essential for effective post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). This study aimed to identify independent factors associated with care-seeking delay and to map the full PEP pathway. METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled 27,930 patients attending the rabies PEP clinic at Santan Hospital, Tianjin, between February 2022 and January 2026. Delay was defined as >12 h from exposure to registration. Multivariable logistic regression, combined with XGBoost and SHAP, identified independent factors for delay and quantified their relative importance. Restricted cubic splines examined the non-linear relationship between age and delay. Subgroup analysis assessed the stability of the association of grade III exposure with more prompt care-seeking. A Sankey diagram traced the PEP pathway. RESULTS: The delay rate was 29.7%. Eight independent factors were identified. Adults had a 34% higher risk of delay than children (aOR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.22-1.47, P < 0.001). Grade III exposure was associated with more prompt care-seeking (aOR = 0.69, 95% CI: 0.65-0.73, P < 0.001). Previous rabies vaccination (aOR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.11-1.23, P < 0.001) and inadequate wound management (aOR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.31-1.88, P < 0.001) were associated with higher delay risk. Age showed a non-linear relationship with delay risk, with adults at highest risk. The Sankey diagram showed that inadequate wound management was rare in the PEP pathway, and the two-dose booster schedule achieved a much higher completion rate than the standard schedule. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that adults may face the highest risk of care-seeking delay, and that improving healthcare access for adults and promoting simplified vaccination schedules may be key to improving PEP quality.

title: Rabies in Military Personnel: Epidemiology, Clinical Challenges, and Strategies for Prevention and Management
abstract: For deployed military personnel, a single exposure from a rabies-infected animal can become a death sentence. With a case fatality rate approaching 100%, rabies remains a serious, yet insufficiently acknowledged hazard for service members, for whom prevention in operational environments poses unique challenges. We conducted a systematic literature search to identify relevant studies on rabies risk in armed forces personnel. By analysing rabies-related fatalities in the military, this review highlights the operational challenges posed by animal bites during deployment, including underreporting and delayed access to care, which compromise timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) administration. Special emphasis is placed on prevention strategies, including pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and animal control protocols tailored to military settings. Its aim is to provide a comprehensive, evidence-based resource for healthcare professionals involved in the protection of deployed forces against this ancient yet still deadly infectious disease.

We conducted a systematic literature search to identify relevant studies on rabies risk in armed forces personnel. By analysing rabies-related fatalities in the military, this review highlights the operational challenges posed by animal bites during deployment, including underreporting and delayed access to care, which compromise timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) administration. Special emphasis is placed on prevention strategies, including pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and animal control protocols tailored to military settings. Its aim is to provide a comprehensive, evidence-based resource for healthcare professionals involved in the protection of deployed forces against this ancient yet still deadly infectious disease.

title: Zoonotic disease risk perceptions associated with commercial wildlife activities in Southeast Asia: A scoping review
abstract: Abstract Background : Zoonotic disease emergence is closely linked to human-wildlife interactions, particularly in commercial wildlife activities where livelihoods, conservation, and health intersect. In Southeast Asia, wildlife hunting, trade, and farming remain integral to many communities, yet limited evidence has been synthesized on how communities engaged in these activities perceive associated zoonotic disease risks. This scoping review examines community perceptions of zoonotic disease risks associated with commercial wildlife activities and explores their implications for One Health research and practice. Methods : Peer-reviewed studies published in English between 2000 and 2024 were identified through PubMed and Google Scholar. Eligible studies examining community perceptions of health or zoonotic disease risks associated with wildlife hunting, trade, farming, or consumption in Southeast Asia were included in the review. Data were extracted and analyzed thematically to identify patterns, knowledge gaps, and implications for research and practice. Results : Eight studies from Thailand, Indonesia, the Lao People’s Democratic Republic, and Myanmar met the inclusion criteria. Studies used qualitative or mixed-methods approaches involving hunters, traders, farmers, consumers, and communities with wildlife contact. Study findings showed partial awareness of zoonotic risks among study populations, often limited to diseases such as avian influenza and rabies. Gaps in translating awareness into preventive practices were highlighted, driven by livelihood dependence, poverty, limited access to services and facilities, and broader structural constraints. Cultural beliefs, gender, and education also shaped risk perceptions and responses, and illegal or informal trade contexts complicated engagement and data collection. Conclusions : Community perceptions of zoonotic disease risk in Southeast Asia are shaped by intersecting social, economic, cultural, and livelihood factors. Effective strategies to reduce zoonotic disease risk associated with commercial wildlife activities require cross-sectoral, context-sensitive approaches that integrate community perspectives into communication and services across the conservation, public health, agriculture, and veterinary sectors. Risk reduction strategies should also move beyond awareness raising to address structural barriers that limit communities’ access to relevant information and services, thereby supporting more equitable and sustainable zoonotic disease prevention in Southeast Asia. One Health impact statement This scoping review highlights the importance of understanding how communities engaged in commercial wildlife activities perceive zoonotic disease risks at the human-animal-environment interfaces in Southeast Asia. By synthesizing limited evidence across health, social, and ecological dimensions, the review demonstrates that awareness of zoonotic disease risks alone is often insufficient to support preventive practices when livelihood dependence, limited access to services, sociocultural beliefs, and broader structural barriers shape decision-making and behaviors. The findings underscore the importance of integrating community perspectives into One Health research and implementation through context-sensitive, cross-sectoral approaches involving conservation, public health, agriculture, and veterinary sectors. While community perceptions alone do not constitute transdisciplinary One Health practice, understanding local experiences, priorities, and constraints provides a critical foundation for coproducing more equitable, culturally grounded, and sustainable zoonotic disease prevention strategies.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Background : Zoonotic disease emergence is closely linked to human-wildlife interactions, particularly in commercial wildlife activities where livelihoods, conservation, and health intersect. In Southeast Asia, wildlife hunting, trade, and farming remain integral to many communities, yet limited evidence has been synthesized on how communities engaged in these activities perceive associated zoonotic disease risks. This scoping review examines community perceptions of zoonotic disease risks associated with commercial wildlife activities and explores their implications for One Health research and practice. Methods : Peer-reviewed studies published in English between 2000 and 2024 were identified through PubMed and Google Scholar. Eligible studies examining community perceptions of health or zoonotic disease risks associated with wildlife hunting, trade, farming, or consumption in Southeast Asia were included in the review. Data were extracted and analyzed thematically to identify patterns, knowledge gaps, and implications for research and practice. Results : Eight studies from Thailand, Indonesia, the Lao People’s Democratic Republic, and Myanmar met the inclusion criteria. Studies used qualitative or mixed-methods approaches involving hunters, traders, farmers, consumers, and communities with wildlife contact. Study findings showed partial awareness of zoonotic risks among study populations, often limited to diseases such as avian influenza and rabies. Gaps in translating awareness into preventive practices were highlighted, driven by livelihood dependence, poverty, limited access to services and facilities, and broader structural constraints. Cultural beliefs, gender, and education also shaped risk perceptions and responses, and illegal or informal trade contexts complicated engagement and data collection. Conclusions : Community perceptions of zoonotic disease risk in Southeast Asia are shaped by intersecting social, economic, cultural, and livelihood factors. Effective strategies to reduce zoonotic disease risk associated with commercial wildlife activities require cross-sectoral, context-sensitive approaches that integrate community perspectives into communication and services across the conservation, public health, agriculture, and veterinary sectors. Risk reduction strategies should also move beyond awareness raising to address structural barriers that limit communities’ access to relevant information and services, thereby supporting more equitable and sustainable zoonotic disease prevention in Southeast Asia. One Health impact statement This scoping review highlights the importance of understanding how communities engaged in commercial wildlife activities perceive zoonotic disease risks at the human-animal-environment interfaces in Southeast Asia. By synthesizing limited evidence across health, social, and ecological dimensions, the review demonstrates that awareness of zoonotic disease risks alone is often insufficient to support preventive practices when livelihood dependence, limited access to services, sociocultural beliefs, and broader structural barriers shape decision-making and behaviors. The findings underscore the importance of integrating community perspectives into One Health research and implementation through context-sensitive, cross-sectoral approaches involving conservation, public health, agriculture, and veterinary sectors. While community perceptions alone do not constitute transdisciplinary One Health practice, understanding local experiences, priorities, and constraints provides a critical foundation for coproducing more equitable, culturally grounded, and sustainable zoonotic disease prevention strategies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 人兽共患病的出现与人类-野生动物互动密切相关,尤其是在商业野生动物活动中,生计、保护与健康在此交汇。本综述研究社区对商业野生动物活动所致人兽共患病风险的认知,并探讨其对‘一个健康’研究与实践的启示。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 通过 PubMed 和 Google Scholar 确定了 2000 年至 2024 年间以英文发表的同行评审研究。审查中纳入了符合条件的研究,该研究考察了社区对东南亚野生动物狩猎、贸易、农业或消费相关的健康或人畜共患疾病风险的看法。数据被提取并按主题进行分析,以确定模式、知识差距以及对研究和实践的影响。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究结果显示,研究人群对人畜共患风险的认识有限,通常仅限于禽流感和 狂犬病 等疾病。东南亚社区对人畜共患疾病风险的看法是由社会、经济、文化和生计等交叉因素决定的。当生计依赖、获得服务的机会有限、社会文化信仰和更广泛的结构性障碍影响决策和行为时,仅对人畜共患疾病风险的认识往往不足以支持预防措施。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 由于生计依赖、贫困、获得服务和设施的机会有限以及更广泛的结构性限制,在将认识转化为预防实践方面存在着差距。文化信仰、性别和教育也影响了风险认知和应对措施,非法或非正式贸易环境使参与和数据收集变得复杂。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 减少与野生动物商业活动相关的人畜共患疾病风险的有效策略需要采取跨部门、因地制宜的方法,将社区观点纳入保护、公共卫生、农业和兽医部门的沟通和服务中。降低风险战略还应超越提高认识的范围,解决限制社区获取相关信息和服务的结构性障碍,从而支持东南亚更加公平和可持续的人畜共患疾病预防。

title: Passive Immunization Hesitancy Among Rabies-Exposed Individuals in China: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: Rabies is an almost universally fatal disease for which post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), including passive immunization (PI) with rabies immunoglobulin or monoclonal antibodies, remains the only effective intervention. Despite established clinical guidelines, real-world PI utilization remains suboptimal. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and determinants of PI hesitancy among previously unvaccinated patients with Category III rabies exposure in China. Methods: This multicenter cross-sectional questionnaire study was conducted at 12 rabies PEP clinics or emergency departments in 12 provinces of mainland China. The analysis included 585 previously unvaccinated adults with Category III rabies exposure who initially hesitated to receive or declined PI. The questionnaire collected sociodemographic characteristics, exposure profiles, awareness of the early protection gap, reasons for initial PI hesitancy or refusal, the decision to receive PI during the same clinical encounter, and PI product selection. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with PI treatment decisions, with results reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs); reason-specific models used the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate correction. All inferential analyses were restricted to adults. Results: Among 5068 eligible previously unvaccinated patients with Category III rabies exposure, 2866 (57%) initially hesitated to receive or declined recommended PI. Of 617 questionnaire respondents, 32 minors were excluded, leaving 585 adults for all inferential analyses. The leading reasons for initial hesitancy were lack of understanding of the immediate protective role of PI (199/585, 34%), belief that vaccination alone was sufficient (194/585, 33%), and high cost (178/585, 30%). During the same clinical encounter, 320/585 adults (55%) chose to receive PI. Awareness of the early protection gap (aOR 2.63, 95% CI 1.75–3.98, p < 0.001) and bachelor’s degree or higher (aOR 1.61, 95% CI 1.07–2.43, p = 0.023) were positively associated with the decision to receive PI, whereas head/face wounds were negatively associated (aOR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30–0.92, p = 0.026). In reason-specific models, lack of knowledge about immediate protection was associated with higher odds of choosing PI (aOR 2.43, 95% CI 1.62–3.68, BH-FDR p < 0.001), whereas high cost was associated with lower odds (aOR 0.41, 95% CI 0.27–0.62, BH-FDR p < 0.001). Conclusion: Hesitancy toward and refusal of PI were observed among previously unvaccinated adults with Category III rabies exposure, yet initial hesitation or refusal is not irreversible. Early protection gap awareness was positively associated with PI choice, whereas cost-related concern was negatively associated. Clear explanation of protection timing and attention to cost-related barriers may support informed PI treatment decisions.

This study aimed to investigate whether reported vaccination coverage translates into actual humoral immunity and examine community knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) that underpin rabies control efforts.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An across-sectional study was conducted between August 2024 and September 2025 across Kitui County (n = 322 households) and Nairobi (n = 276 households), comprising 598 household surveys administered via Kobo Collect. analysis.methods: The study used a validated competitive ELISA (Platelia® Rabies II) to measure rabies virus-neutralizing antibodies (RVNA) against the WHO/WOAH protective threshold of ≥ 0.5 IU/ml. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of biological seroprotection as a more accurate metric for rabies control than administrative vaccination coverage, with implications for surveillance and intervention strategies in Kenya.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between reported vaccination coverage and actual seroprotection against rabies in rural and urban Kenya. It highlights a vaccination paradox where high reported coverage does not equate to sufficient biological immunity. The research underscores the importance of biological monitoring over administrative data for effective rabies control. The study's findings suggest that community knowledge and attitudes play a critical role in rabies prevention. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and a limited sample size of canine serum samples may affect the strength of its conclusions. The results have implications for improving surveillance and intervention strategies in Kenya.

title: Design and Assembly of Combinatorial DNA Barcodes for Probe-based Genomics Applications
abstract: Probe-based genomics technologies are extending molecular analysis into intact tissues and fixed cells, yet strategies to decode complex experimental conditions encoded in cellular RNA remain limited. Here we present a modular framework that integrates custom software tools with purpose-built cloning reagents to design, assemble, validate, and deploy combinatorial DNA barcodes. Combinatorial barcodes comprise spatially adjacent collections of known sequences, enabling millions of unique molecules to be efficiently distinguished using a limited set of probes. Our software tools integrate with optimized assembly plasmids and whole plasmid long-read sequencing for high-fidelity construction and structural validation of diverse combinatorial barcode architectures. Assembled barcode libraries are flexibly transferred into user-modified expression vectors to support diverse downstream experimental applications. We showcase the versatility of this framework by assembling two structurally distinct combinatorial barcode libraries, each containing millions of unique sequences. Following rabies virus-based delivery to the mouse brain, we validate in vivo decoding of a combinatorial barcode architecture capable of distinguishing ~16.3 million expressed RNAs through probe-based in situ sequencing. Our framework for flexible and accurate combinatorial barcode construction fills a technically demanding niche delivering cost-effective molecular reagents for multiplexed experimentation on current and evolving probe-based genomics platforms.

title: Untargeted metabolomics reveals metabolic reprogramming and key metabolites in adherent and suspension Vero cells
abstract: Introduction Vero cells are the primary host for industrial vaccine production, and high-density suspension culture is the predominant manufacturing approach. However, this method faces major challenges, including low shear tolerance, difficulty adapting to serum-free conditions, metabolic imbalance, prolonged acclimation periods, and batch-to-batch variability. Furthermore, the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying suspension adaptation remain poorly understood. Methods We established serum-free suspension adaptation of adherent Vero cells using reduction serum levels strategy. Biological characteristics of suspension-adapted cells were analyzed through morphological observation, cell viability assays, and karyotyping. A recombinant rabies vesicular stomatitis virus infection model was used to assess viral susceptibility and replication capacity. Untargeted liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry metabolomics was then utilized to systematically characterize intracellular metabolic profiles of Vero cells cultured under adherent and suspension conditions. Differential metabolites were identified, and key regulatory pathways were evaluated to elucidate the metabolic mechanisms of suspension adaptation and identify potential optimization targets. Results Suspension-adapted Vero cells exhibited uniform morphology, stable genetic characteristics, and robust proliferative capacity, without evidence of degeneration or mutation. Viral sensitivity assays demonstrated efficient viral adsorption and replication, yielding stable viral titers and confirming suitability for vaccine production. Metabolomic analysis identified 119 metabolites (32 upregulated, 47 downregulated, and 40 unchanged), with significant enrichment in alanine/aspartate/glutamate metabolism, glycine/serine/threonine metabolism, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Suspension cells displayed Warburg-like metabolic features, including enhanced glycolysis, increased lactate accumulation, and pronounced upregulation of succinate and malate. L-serine and ethanolamine phosphate were strongly upregulated, whereas polyunsaturated fatty acids were significantly reduced. Suspension adaptation involved coordinated remodeling of energy, amino acid, nucleotide, and lipid metabolism; enhancing shear tolerance through membrane lipid remodeling; improving antioxidant capacity via serine metabolism; and supporting high-density proliferation through glycolytic reprogramming. Discussion This study established a serum-free suspension adaptation system for Vero cells with stable phenotypic characteristics and high viral susceptibility while elucidating metabolic regulatory mechanisms that underlie suspension adaptation. The findings provide metabolic targets and a theoretical foundation for rational medium design, targeted supplementation strategies, and development of genetically engineered cell lines with enhanced shear resistance.

title_zh: 非靶向代谢组学揭示贴壁和悬浮 Vero 细胞中的代谢重编程和关键代谢物
source_body_en: Introduction Vero cells are the primary host for industrial vaccine production, and high-density suspension culture is the predominant manufacturing approach. However, this method faces major challenges, including low shear tolerance, difficulty adapting to serum-free conditions, metabolic imbalance, prolonged acclimation periods, and batch-to-batch variability. Furthermore, the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying suspension adaptation remain poorly understood. Methods We established serum-free suspension adaptation of adherent Vero cells using reduction serum levels strategy. Biological characteristics of suspension-adapted cells were analyzed through morphological observation, cell viability assays, and karyotyping. A recombinant rabies vesicular stomatitis virus infection model was used to assess viral susceptibility and replication capacity. Untargeted liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry metabolomics was then utilized to systematically characterize intracellular metabolic profiles of Vero cells cultured under adherent and suspension conditions. Differential metabolites were identified, and key regulatory pathways were evaluated to elucidate the metabolic mechanisms of suspension adaptation and identify potential optimization targets. Results Suspension-adapted Vero cells exhibited uniform morphology, stable genetic characteristics, and robust proliferative capacity, without evidence of degeneration or mutation. Viral sensitivity assays demonstrated efficient viral adsorption and replication, yielding stable viral titers and confirming suitability for vaccine production. Metabolomic analysis identified 119 metabolites (32 upregulated, 47 downregulated, and 40 unchanged), with significant enrichment in alanine/aspartate/glutamate metabolism, glycine/serine/threonine metabolism, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Suspension cells displayed Warburg-like metabolic features, including enhanced glycolysis, increased lactate accumulation, and pronounced upregulation of succinate and malate. L-serine and ethanolamine phosphate were strongly upregulated, whereas polyunsaturated fatty acids were significantly reduced. Suspension adaptation involved coordinated remodeling of energy, amino acid, nucleotide, and lipid metabolism; enhancing shear tolerance through membrane lipid remodeling; improving antioxidant capacity via serine metabolism; and supporting high-density proliferation through glycolytic reprogramming. Discussion This study established a serum-free suspension adaptation system for Vero cells with stable phenotypic characteristics and high viral susceptibility while elucidating metabolic regulatory mechanisms that underlie suspension adaptation. The findings provide metabolic targets and a theoretical foundation for rational medium design, targeted supplementation strategies, and development of genetically engineered cell lines with enhanced shear resistance.
abstract_zh: 引言 Vero细胞是工业化疫苗生产的主要宿主,高密度悬浮培养是主流制造工艺。然而,该方法面临多重挑战,包括低剪切耐受性、难以适应无血清条件、代谢失衡、长期驯化周期及批次间差异。此外,悬浮适应背后的代谢重编程机制尚不清楚。方法 本研究通过逐步降低血清水平策略,建立了贴壁Vero细胞的无血清悬浮适应系统。通过形态观察、细胞活力检测及核型分析,对悬浮适应细胞的生物学特性进行表征。利用重组狂犬病水泡性口炎病毒感染模型,评估病毒易感性及复制能力。随后采用非靶向液相色谱-串联质谱代谢组学,系统解析贴壁与悬浮培养条件下Vero细胞的细胞内代谢谱。识别差异代谢物,并评估关键调控通路,以阐明悬浮适应的代谢机制并挖掘潜在优化靶点。结果 悬浮适应Vero细胞形态均一、遗传特性稳定、增殖能力强,未见退化或突变现象。病毒敏感性检测显示其对病毒的吸附与复制效率高,稳定产毒且适于疫苗生产。代谢组学分析共鉴定出119个代谢物(32个上调、47个下调、40个无显著变化),显著富集于丙氨酸/天冬氨酸/谷氨酸代谢、甘氨酸/丝氨酸/苏氨酸代谢及三羧酸循环。悬浮细胞呈现Warburg样代谢特征,包括增强的糖酵解、乳酸积累增加及琥珀酸与苹果酸的显著上调。L-丝氨酸与乙醇胺磷酸强烈上调,而多不饱和脂肪酸显著下调。悬浮适应涉及能量、氨基酸、核苷酸及脂质代谢的协同重塑;通过膜脂质重塑增强剪切耐受;通过丝氨酸代谢提升抗氧化能力;并通过糖酵解重编程支持高密度增殖。讨论 本研究建立了无血清悬浮适应Vero细胞系统,其表型特征稳定且病毒易感性高,同时阐明了悬浮适应的代谢调控机制。研究结果为合理培养基设计、靶向营养补充策略及构建高剪切抗性工程细胞株提供了代谢靶点与理论基础。

full_text: Based on multiple instances of human-to-human rabies transmission via organ or tissue transplantation from initially undiagnosed rabies-infected donors, we estimate 856 (213–2220) human rabies deaths in the United States (US) from 2000 to 2024, meaning that only around 7% of human rabies deaths in the US were confirmed during this period. Subjects Article PDF In February 2025, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) of the United States (US) diagnosed rabies in a kidney transplant recipient and subsequently in the donor who died in December 20241. This event marks the fourth transplant-related rabies transmission from an initially undiagnosed donor in the US since 1978, following transmission events identified from the three earlier donors—who died in 19782, 20043, and 20114—which resulted in six deaths, in one cornea recipient, three kidney recipients, one liver recipient and one arterial-segment recipient. In each case transplantation was allowed because rabies had not been diagnosed in the deceased donor before organ or tissue transplantation. Additional transplant recipients from these donors remained asymptomatic following post-exposure prophylaxis1,4. Each year, very few rabies cases have been confirmed in the US, including Puerto Rico, on average 2.4 per annum from 2000 to 2024 (Fig. 1 and Supplementary Data)5. However, the instances of rabies transmission from initially undiagnosed deceased donors suggest that many human deaths due to rabies are not diagnosed as such, considering that only a small percentage of people dying in the US become organ and tissue donors. An estimate of the number of human deaths in the US due to undiagnosed rabies in the 25 years from 2000 to 2024 can be obtained from the identified number of deceased donors who died of rabies undiagnosed prior to transplantation1,3,4 (n = 3) divided by the number of deceased donors (n = 239,251, Fig. 1) and multiplied by the number of deaths (n = 68,266,224, Fig. 1) (see Supplementary Data for data sources and estimation). The underlying assumption is that donors have experienced the average national risk of rabies infection. This gives an estimate of 856 (95% CI: 213–2220) undiagnosed human rabies deaths over the 25-year period in the US, corresponding to an average of 34.2 (95% CI: 8.5–88.8) deaths per annum. Our central estimate suggests that only around 7% (i.e. 0.07 = 2.4/36.6 deaths per annum) of human rabies cases in the general population were confirmed in recent years, and even its confidence limits indicate that, in the best-case scenario, only around 22% were diagnosed. In order to argue that the reported number of rabies cases is consistent with complete surveillance, deceased donors would need to have a rabies risk approximately 14 times that of decedents in the general population. Both the risk of rabies infection and the probability of becoming a donor after death might be associated with geographical, occupational, and socioeconomic factors. Therefore, data on predictors of rabies infection and donation after death would help refine our estimate. While canine rabies is notoriously under-detected in affected countries6, our estimate highlights that under-detection of human cases could also occur in countries in which rabies risk is limited mostly to wildlife exposure. The long and variable incubation period, ranging weeks to one year7, likely contributes to under-detection in the US. Additionally, a substantial number of exposures may go either unobserved (e.g. non-apparent injuries) or unrecognised as posing a rabies risk (e.g. superficial scratches or a general lack of risk awareness in the region of residence or travel)8. Consequently, substantial under-detection in the general population may both result from and contribute to an underappreciation of rabies transmission, thereby sustaining ongoing transmission risks to transplant recipients. Although these factors would also contribute to under-detection in canine-rabies-endemic countries, their exact mechanisms and relative contributions likely differ from those in the US, given differing diagnostic capacities and rabies risk profiles (i.e. exposure to wildlife versus free-roaming or owned dogs). Our results highlight the need to enhance rabies diagnosis, for example, by increasing risk awareness in the public, obtaining in-depth exposure histories, considering potential geographical, occupational, and socioeconomic risk factors independently of exposure histories, and explicitly including rabies among the differential diagnoses for patients who die from unexplained clinical signs compatible with rabies, including encephalitis. full_text_sections.full_text: Based on multiple instances of human-to-human rabies transmission via organ or tissue transplantation from initially undiagnosed rabies-infected donors, we estimate 856 (213–2220) human rabies deaths in the United States (US) from 2000 to 2024, meaning that only around 7% of human rabies deaths in the US were confirmed during this period. Subjects Article PDF In February 2025, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) of the United States (US) diagnosed rabies in a kidney transplant recipient and subsequently in the donor who died in December 20241. This event marks the fourth transplant-related rabies transmission from an initially undiagnosed donor in the US since 1978, following transmission events identified from the three earlier donors—who died in 19782, 20043, and 20114—which resulted in six deaths, in one cornea recipient, three kidney recipients, one liver recipient and one arterial-segment recipient. In each case transplantation was allowed because rabies had not been diagnosed in the deceased donor before organ or tissue transplantation. Additional transplant recipients from these donors remained asymptomatic following post-exposure prophylaxis1,4. Each year, very few rabies cases have been confirmed in the US, including Puerto Rico, on average 2.4 per annum from 2000 to 2024 (Fig. 1 and Supplementary Data)5. However, the instances of rabies transmission from initially undiagnosed deceased donors suggest that many human deaths due to rabies are not diagnosed as such, considering that only a small percentage of people dying in the US become organ and tissue donors. An estimate of the number of human deaths in the US due to undiagnosed rabies in the 25 years from 2000 to 2024 can be obtained from the identified number of deceased donors who died of rabies undiagnosed prior to transplantation1,3,4 (n = 3) divided by the number of deceased donors (n = 239,251, Fig. 1) and multiplied by the number of deaths (n = 68,266,224, Fig. 1) (see Supplementary Data for data sources and estimation). The underlying assumption is that donors have experienced the average national risk of rabies infection. This gives an estimate of 856 (95% CI: 213–2220) undiagnosed human rabies deaths over the 25-year period in the US, corresponding to an average of 34.2 (95% CI: 8.5–88.8) deaths per annum. Our central estimate suggests that only around 7% (i.e. 0.07 = 2.4/36.6 deaths per annum) of human rabies cases in the general population were confirmed in recent years, and even its confidence limits indicate that, in the best-case scenario, only around 22% were diagnosed. In order to argue that the reported number of rabies cases is consistent with complete surveillance, deceased donors would need to have a rabies risk approximately 14 times that of decedents in the general population. Both the risk of rabies infection and the probability of becoming a donor after death might be associated with geographical, occupational, and socioeconomic factors. Therefore, data on predictors of rabies infection and donation after death would help refine our estimate. While canine rabies is notoriously under-detected in affected countries6, our estimate highlights that under-detection of human cases could also occur in countries in which rabies risk is limited mostly to wildlife exposure. The long and variable incubation period, ranging weeks to one year7, likely contributes to under-detection in the US. Additionally, a substantial number of exposures may go either unobserved (e.g. non-apparent injuries) or unrecognised as posing a rabies risk (e.g. superficial scratches or a general lack of risk awareness in the region of residence or travel)8. Consequently, substantial under-detection in the general population may both result from and contribute to an underappreciation of rabies transmission, thereby sustaining ongoing transmission risks to transplant recipients. Although these factors would also contribute to under-detection in canine-rabies-endemic countries, their exact mechanisms and relative contributions likely differ from those in the US, given differing diagnostic capacities and rabies risk profiles (i.e. exposure to wildlife versus free-roaming or owned dogs). Our results highlight the need to enhance rabies diagnosis, for example, by increasing risk awareness in the public, obtaining in-depth exposure histories, considering potential geographical, occupational, and socioeconomic risk factors independently of exposure histories, and explicitly including rabies among the differential diagnoses for patients who die from unexplained clinical signs compatible with rabies, including encephalitis. title_original: Substantial under-detection of human rabies cases in the United States

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the under-detection of human rabies cases in the United States, highlighting the risk of undiagnosed rabies infections in deceased donors leading to transmission via organ or tissue transplantation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed rabies transmission events from 2000 to 2024, focusing on cases where rabies was transmitted through organ or tissue transplantation from donors who were not diagnosed with rabies before death. It included data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and other sources.
analysis.methods: The researchers estimated the number of undiagnosed rabies deaths by dividing the number of identified rabies-related donor deaths by the total number of deceased donors and multiplying by the total number of deaths in the US. They assumed that donors had the average national risk of rabies infection.
analysis.main_results: The study found that only around 7% of human rabies deaths in the US were confirmed between 2000 and 2024, with an estimated 856 (95% CI: 213–2220) deaths due to undiagnosed rabies. This corresponds to an average of 34.2 (95% CI: 8.5–88.8) deaths per year.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of substantial under-detection of rabies cases in the US, emphasizing that the current surveillance system may not capture the true burden of the disease due to the low rate of rabies diagnosis in deceased donors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that the existing surveillance system for rabies in the US significantly underestimates the number of human rabies deaths, which has important implications for improving diagnostic practices and donor screening protocols.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on the assumption that donors have the average national risk of rabies infection, which may not account for geographical, occupational, or socioeconomic variations. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on reported cases and extrapolation.

analysis.summary_en: This study highlights the under-detection of human rabies cases in the United States, estimating that 856 (95% CI: 213–2220) deaths occurred due to undiagnosed rabies infections in deceased donors between 2000 and 2024. Only around 7% of these deaths were confirmed, indicating a significant gap in surveillance. The study analyzed rabies transmission events through organ or tissue transplantation, noting that four such cases have been identified since 1978. The authors suggest that the current diagnostic system fails to capture the true burden of rabies, as only a small percentage of deaths lead to organ donation. The findings emphasize the need for improved donor screening and diagnostic practices to prevent future transmission. However, the study's estimate is based on assumptions about donor risk and may not account for all variables, limiting its strength.
